documents.title: Georgia State University Artificial Intelligence Policy
documents.stance_why: The policy sets no student-facing allow or ban rule; it says "Class use of AI tools shall be at the discretion of the instructor" and sets principles, data rules and reporting around it, so the stance is delegates.
documents.summary: GSU's institution-wide AI policy sets principles, data-protection and tool-vetting rules, disclosure, misuse reporting, definitions and governance. It leaves class-level decisions to instructors, and its detailed student and faculty disclosure standards sit in an unfetched supplement.

units.why: The introduction states the policy's purpose: "guide the GSU community in the ethical use of emerging technologies". An institution-level purpose statement is P56, addressed to everyone, general, informs.
units.anchor: guide the GSU community in the ethical use of emerging technologies

units.why: "USG policy controls" sets the hierarchy between this policy and the system policy, a framework/scope statement, so P56, informs.
units.anchor: In the event of any conﬂict, USG policy controls.

units.why: The purpose section says the policy gives "a framework for the responsible and ethical integration of AI technologies"; this is the institution-wide framework type P56.
units.anchor: provide a framework for the responsible and ethical integration of AI technologies

units.why: The supplement "may be updated by the AI Committee as needed" to address technological developments; this signals the guidance will change, so P54, informs.
units.anchor: may be updated by the AI Committee as needed

units.why: The section opens a list of eight guiding principles ("Protection", "Compliance", ...) for AI adoption and use; a principles preamble is P56. The list is coded as one unit, with disclosure and review pulled out separately.
units.anchor: Key principles from the University System of Georgia for the use of AI are:
units.frag_end: for the use of AI are:
units.policy: The policy adopts principles from the University System of Georgia for AI use: protection, compliance, focus, purposed, performance, vigilance, inventoried and human-informed.

units.why: The Human-Informed principle says "such use shall be appropriately disclosed and transparent"; a binding disclosure duty for AI use, so P24, must, addressed to all.
units.anchor: such use shall be appropriately disclosed and transparent

units.why: The Performance principle calls for "Periodically reviewing results with stakeholders" to check AI is meeting objectives, a review cycle; P54 rather than P55 because it is about the institution's AI adoption, not learning evidence.
units.anchor: Periodically reviewing results with stakeholders to ensure AI is successfully meeting objectives.

units.why: "Final responsibility ... rests with the individuals using it" puts accountability for AI use on each user, so P29 (owning what you submit/use) fits better than P31, which is about verifying output.
units.anchor: Final responsibility for the appropriate use of AI and its compliance with GSU and USG

units.why: Faculty, staff and students "are expected to uphold the highest standards of integrity", a general principle of ethical AI use, so P56 rather than a specific misconduct type.
units.anchor: expected to uphold the highest standards of integrity and foster honest scholarship
units.frag_start: GSU faculty, staff, and students are

units.why: "appropriate precautions should be given to the sensitive information or protected data being input into AI tools" is a data-protection duty, so P50, should.
units.anchor: Consideration and appropriate precautions should be given to the sensitive information or protected data being

units.why: "steps should be taken to account for bias and ensure accuracy" of AI outputs is a verify-the-output duty; P31 covers bias and accuracy checking.
units.anchor: steps should be taken to account for bias and ensure accuracy
units.frag_start: Also, steps should be taken to

units.why: Sensitive or confidential data "should not be used in or provided to AI tools"; a restriction on what data goes into AI, P50, should-not as worded.
units.anchor: should not be used in or provided to AI tools
units.policy: Data classified as sensitive or confidential should not be used in or provided to AI tools.

units.why: If the AI Committee grants an exception, sensitive data "may be used only in University approved AI tools", a vetted-tool condition on data use, so P50, may.
units.anchor: may be used only in University approved AI tools

units.why: "AI tools must only collect, process, and store data according to the tool's approved use" is a binding data-handling requirement, P50.
units.anchor: AI tools must only collect, process, and store data according to the tool’s approved use.

units.why: "Data minimization and transparency must be prioritized" is a data-protection rule, P50, must.
units.anchor: Data minimization and transparency must be prioritized when using AI to process data.

units.why: Faculty and staff "must select from the IIT list of approved options", requiring vetted tools; P50 (prefer vetted tools), addressed to instructors.
units.anchor: they must select from the IIT list of approved options
units.frag_start: If faculty and staff use AI tools
units.policy: Faculty and staff who use AI tools for academic and professional work must select from the IIT list of approved options.

units.why: "should be properly disclosed and cited" states a general disclosure and citation expectation for AI use, P24, should.
units.anchor: AI use in academic and professional work should be properly disclosed and cited.
units.frag_start: AI use in academic and professional

units.why: "Research uses of AI are subject to existing data protection rules, IRB approval processes" defers research AI use to existing rules, which is P62.
units.anchor: Research uses of AI are subject to existing data protection rules, IRB approval processes

units.anchor: syllabus production guidelines that address AI

units.policy: Instructors' class AI rules should be consistent with GSU guidance, including syllabus production guidelines that address AI, and the student code of conduct.

units.why: "must monitor and validate AI tools to ensure they produce results as intended" is a verification duty for faculty and staff, P31.
units.anchor: Faculty and staff must monitor and validate AI tools to ensure they produce results as

units.why: "must be reported to IIT and addressed promptly" is an incident-reporting duty for AI tool problems. It is not data protection (P50) or output verification (P31) itself, so UNCOVERED.
units.anchor: Any discrepancies or issues must be reported to IIT and addressed promptly.
units.uncovered_note: Duty to report AI tool discrepancies or issues to IIT

units.why: Individuals "are responsible for the completeness and accuracy of their work", "verifying the accuracy of information generated by AI"; P31 (verify AI output) is chosen over P29 because the specific duty is verification.
units.anchor: This includes verifying the accuracy of information generated by AI

units.why: "Users must respect intellectual property rights" and keep generated content within legal standards; IP and legal compliance is P52.
units.anchor: Users must respect intellectual property rights
units.policy: Users must respect intellectual property rights and ensure that all content generated complies with legal standards.

units.why: Substantive AI use "must follow the GSU Disclosure Standards" for faculty, staff and students; a mandatory disclosure rule, P24.
units.anchor: faculty, staff, and students must follow the GSU Disclosure Standards
units.frag_start: When AI is used in a
units.policy: When AI is used in a substantive manner for analysis or decision-making, faculty, staff, and students must follow the GSU Disclosure Standards detailed in the AI Policy Supplement.

units.why: "Misuse of AI by campus stakeholders is considered a violation" classifies misuse as a violation handled by reporting channels, P36.
units.anchor: Misuse of AI by campus stakeholders is considered a violation

units.why: The policy defines unintentional misuse ("data exposure ... overdependency on AI, bias, and drift"); a definition of what counts as misuse, grouped with P36 as the classification of misuse. P61 was rejected because it defines AI terms, not misuse.
units.anchor: Unintentional misuse includes actions such as data exposure
units.policy: Unintentional misuse includes data exposure, misleading or incorrect conclusions, inappropriate results, overdependency on AI, bias, and drift.

units.why: Lists intentional misuse ("fraud, invasion of privacy, malicious use"), a definition of misuse feeding the misconduct classification, P36.
units.anchor: Examples of intentional misuse include fraud, invasion of privacy, malicious use

units.why: "Intentional misuse will result in disciplinary action" states a consequence handled through discipline; P36 rather than P37 because no concrete penalty is named.
units.anchor: Intentional misuse will result in disciplinary action.

units.why: The reporting table's Students row routes AI misuse as an "Academic Integrity Violation" to the "Dean of Students"; this is the integrity process for students, P36.
units.anchor: Dean of Students
units.policy: Student AI misuse is an academic integrity violation reported to the Dean of Students.

units.why: The table's Faculty row sends AI misuse as an "Academic Integrity Violation" to the "Department Chair or per Faculty Handbook Procedures"; handled through integrity procedures, P36.
units.anchor: Department Chair or per Faculty Handbook Procedures
units.policy: Faculty AI misuse is an academic integrity violation reported to the Department Chair or per Faculty Handbook Procedures.

units.why: "AI Tool procurement should follow the GSU contract and procurement procedures" concerns institutional review of AI contracts, P65.
units.anchor: AI Tool procurement should follow the GSU contract and procurement procedures

units.why: Warns that "external collaborators' use of AI may put University data at risk" and that safeguards apply to third-party agreements; third-party AI agreements, P65.
units.anchor: external collaborators’ use of AI may put University data at risk
units.policy: Users should be aware that external collaborators' use of AI may put University data at risk.

units.why: "GSU will create and maintain an AI tool inventory" is an institutional administrative commitment; P65 covers contracts and data sharing, not an inventory, so UNCOVERED.
units.anchor: GSU will create and maintain an AI tool inventory.
units.uncovered_note: Institution maintains an inventory of AI tools

units.why: The section sets triggers for "additional University AI Committee review" (new uses, automated decision-making, data types); a review-gate that matches no existing type, so UNCOVERED.

units.frag_start: In certain AI uses, additional University
units.uncovered_note: Committee review required for novel AI uses, automated decisions, and data types

units.policy: Using AI for automated decision-making requires extreme caution and should not be used without consulting with the University AI Committee.

units.why: "Grading or assessment of student work" is listed as an automated-decision example needing committee consultation. It does not say humans must grade, so P59 not P46.

units.policy: Grading or assessment of student work is an example of automated decision-making that requires consulting the University AI Committee.

units.why: "Training on AI will be provided for all GSU community members" is institutional support for learning AI; P63 is the closest type (support in learning AI).

units.why: "Awareness will be achieved through a multi-channel communications strategy" commits to promoting the policy; no type covers policy awareness campaigns, so UNCOVERED.
units.anchor: Awareness will be achieved through a multi-channel communications strategy
units.uncovered_note: Campus-wide awareness and communication strategy about the AI policy

units.why: States scope: applies to "all Georgia State University faculty, staff, and students"; scope statement of an institution-wide framework, P56.
units.anchor: This Policy applies to all Georgia State University faculty, staff, and students.

units.policy: The University AI Committee is responsible for conducting the policy review and for monitoring legal and technical developments in Artificial Intelligence.
